assignments.evidence_note: Atelier Bow-Wow identifies the 2011 Shibuya project as Miyashita Park, designed with Tokyo Institute of Technology Tsukamoto Lab, with a 14,000 square metre park area. This historical 2011 park is distinct from the 2020 MIYASHITA PARK canonical building already in production. The image accurately shows the covered sports and circulation space of the 2011 park; Commons identifies Douglas P. Perkins as the own-work creator and licenses it CC BY 3.0.

Kono Designs identifies Pasona HQ as a nine-storey corporate office renovation integrating offices, auditorium, cafeterias, rooftop garden and urban farming facilities. Mixed-use is approved as the available function that accurately expresses the deliberate office, food, education and farming combination; the broad building type remains office. The local image clearly shows the exact Pasona building and planted facade; Commons identifies 螺钉 own work, 3648 by 2736, CC BY-SA 3.0.

The cooperative describes an affordable modular working environment for creative entrepreneurs, self-built from waste and second-hand materials around a regenerative garden. The official case study explicitly describes a publicly accessible courtyard and social-cultural events, supporting mixed-use primary and public-space secondary while the broad type remains office. The local image accurately shows the circular material facade and courtyard; the Flickr page identifies nandasluijsmans and CC BY-SA 2.0, with an original 3180 by 2580 image.
